### Thread 4 — `js/postTestReworkResults.js` line 279

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `updatePullRequestBody` reports success even when the PATCH fails**

Now that `scm.updatePrBody` is a live seam (gh-960 rework implemented `_githubUpdatePrBody`), it returns `null` when the `gh api` PATCH throws or yields no output — but this caller logs `✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result` and returns `true` regardless:

```javascript
if (scm.updatePrBody) {
    scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
    console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
    return true;
}
```

Non-blocking (the return value isn't consumed and failures stay non-fatal by design), but a `null` result printing a green check is misleading in logs. Consider:

```javascript
var ok = scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
if (ok) console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
else console.warn('PR body update failed — summary comment still posted');
return !!ok;
```

### Thread 5 — `js/common/pullRequest.js` line 203

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION (repost, still valid): `pr.merged === true` is unreachable; ADO `completed` state not covered**

Carrying this over from the previous round — it was not addressed and remains accurate:

- `github_list_prs` (REST list) returns no `merged` field and only `state: 'open'` PRs are listed, so `if (pr.merged === true) return true;` never fires in production — the `ai_validating` label is the only live freeze signal. Harmless defensive code, but a one-line comment saying so would stop readers hunting for the populating call site.
- ADO closes work items/PRs as `completed`, which `state === 'closed' || state === 'merged'` does not match — if this predicate is ever fed ADO-shaped state, it won't freeze. Worth a comment or an explicit `'completed'` arm.

Non-blocking; the shipped behavior is correct for the GitHub path this guards.

## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

2. **Dead seam.** The rewrite being frozen lives in `updatePullRequestBody` behind `scm.updatePrBody` — but no SCM provider implements `updatePrBody` (checked `_createGithubProvider`, `_createGitLabProvider`, `_createAdoProvider` in `js/common/scm.js`; the string appears only in this consumer and in test mocks). In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

I also searched the rest of the tree: no JS code path edits an existing PR body (merge bot, smAgent, pushReworkChanges, developTicketAndCreatePR, postMobileTestAutomationResults all only *read* bodies or post comments). That means the `Closes #952` line landed on #956's body at the merge moment from outside the JS automation — most plausibly an agent session in the finalizing run editing the body via `gh` (the rework/dev legs have `bash` in `CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` and produce `outputs/pr_body.md`).

**Ask:** trace the actual write path for dev PRs and put the freeze there — e.g. a pre/post-JS guard that refuses `gh pr edit --body*` while `ai_validating` is on the PR, or a prompt-level rule in the rework/dev instructions. Alternatively, implement `updatePrBody` on the GitHub provider so the machine owns the body rewrite deterministically and this guard becomes live code. As shipped, the ticket AC ("the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms") is not demonstrably satisfied.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```

gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 3 — `.fah/memory/.gitignore` line 1

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: session memory artifacts leaked into the PR — remove `.fah/memory/`**

This PR ships 9 files under `.fah/memory/` (7 agent memory notes, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`) that have nothing to do with gh-960 — they are `fa` session memory records (dated 2026-10-03/04, topics: development-agent loop gotchas, CI secret-handling notes) captured by the WIP auto-save. `main` deliberately does not track `.fah/` (`.gitignore` line 36, reinforced by b8d09c4e "chore: ignore .fah/ session runtime artifacts"), and this PR itself deletes the sibling `.fah/bash_jobs/*` artifacts as noise.

Beyond scope creep, these files will keep causing exactly the kind of merge friction this PR is already hitting (a live session mutates its memory/jobs state while another branch deletes it). Drop them from the PR (`git rm -r --cached .fah/memory` + commit; keep the working-tree copies locally).

Note: no literal secret is exposed in these notes (the PUSH_TOKEN mention describes interpolation, not a value), but session memory still does not belong in the shared repo tree.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/postTestReworkResults.js` line 279

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `updatePullRequestBody` reports success even when the PATCH fails**

Now that `scm.updatePrBody` is a live seam (gh-960 rework implemented `_githubUpdatePrBody`), it returns `null` when the `gh api` PATCH throws or yields no output — but this caller logs `✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result` and returns `true` regardless:

```javascript
if (scm.updatePrBody) {
    scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
    console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
    return true;
}
```

Non-blocking (the return value isn't consumed and failures stay non-fatal by design), but a `null` result printing a green check is misleading in logs. Consider:

```javascript
var ok = scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
if (ok) console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
else console.warn('PR body update failed — summary comment still posted');
return !!ok;
```

---

### Thread 5 — `js/common/pullRequest.js` line 203

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION (repost, still valid): `pr.merged === true` is unreachable; ADO `completed` state not covered**

Carrying this over from the previous round — it was not addressed and remains accurate:

- `github_list_prs` (REST list) returns no `merged` field and only `state: 'open'` PRs are listed, so `if (pr.merged === true) return true;` never fires in production — the `ai_validating` label is the only live freeze signal. Harmless defensive code, but a one-line comment saying so would stop readers hunting for the populating call site.
- ADO closes work items/PRs as `completed`, which `state === 'closed' || state === 'merged'` does not match — if this predicate is ever fed ADO-shaped state, it won't freeze. Worth a comment or an explicit `'completed'` arm.

Non-blocking; the shipped behavior is correct for the GitHub path this guards.

## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

2. **Dead seam.** The rewrite being frozen lives in `updatePullRequestBody` behind `scm.updatePrBody` — but no SCM provider implements `updatePrBody` (checked `_createGithubProvider`, `_createGitLabProvider`, `_createAdoProvider` in `js/common/scm.js`; the string appears only in this consumer and in test mocks). In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

I also searched the rest of the tree: no JS code path edits an existing PR body (merge bot, smAgent, pushReworkChanges, developTicketAndCreatePR, postMobileTestAutomationResults all only *read* bodies or post comments). That means the `Closes #952` line landed on #956's body at the merge moment from outside the JS automation — most plausibly an agent session in the finalizing run editing the body via `gh` (the rework/dev legs have `bash` in `CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` and produce `outputs/pr_body.md`).

**Ask:** trace the actual write path for dev PRs and put the freeze there — e.g. a pre/post-JS guard that refuses `gh pr edit --body*` while `ai_validating` is on the PR, or a prompt-level rule in the rework/dev instructions. Alternatively, implement `updatePrBody` on the GitHub provider so the machine owns the body rewrite deterministically and this guard becomes live code. As shipped, the ticket AC ("the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms") is not demonstrably satisfied.

Fixed. Extracted the label scan from `isPrBodyFrozen` into a `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels)` helper in `js/common/pullRequest.js`, exactly along the suggested lines. `isPrBodyFrozen` is now a flat predicate (CC ≈ 6 → CRAP ≈ 6 at full coverage) and the helper ≈ 5, both under the gate's threshold of 8. # gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 3 — `.fah/memory/.gitignore` line 1

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: session memory artifacts leaked into the PR — remove `.fah/memory/`**

This PR ships 9 files under `.fah/memory/` (7 agent memory notes, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`) that have nothing to do with gh-960 — they are `fa` session memory records (dated 2026-10-03/04, topics: development-agent loop gotchas, CI secret-handling notes) captured by the WIP auto-save. `main` deliberately does not track `.fah/` (`.gitignore` line 36, reinforced by b8d09c4e "chore: ignore .fah/ session runtime artifacts"), and this PR itself deletes the sibling `.fah/bash_jobs/*` artifacts as noise.

Beyond scope creep, these files will keep causing exactly the kind of merge friction this PR is already hitting (a live session mutates its memory/jobs state while another branch deletes it). Drop them from the PR (`git rm -r --cached .fah/memory` + commit; keep the working-tree copies locally).

Note: no literal secret is exposed in these notes (the PUSH_TOKEN mention describes interpolation, not a value), but session memory still does not belong in the shared repo tree.

### Thread 4 — `js/postTestReworkResults.js` line 279

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `updatePullRequestBody` reports success even when the PATCH fails**

Now that `scm.updatePrBody` is a live seam (gh-960 rework implemented `_githubUpdatePrBody`), it returns `null` when the `gh api` PATCH throws or yields no output — but this caller logs `✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result` and returns `true` regardless:

```javascript
if (scm.updatePrBody) {
    scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
    console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
    return true;
}
```

Non-blocking (the return value isn't consumed and failures stay non-fatal by design), but a `null` result printing a green check is misleading in logs. Consider:

```javascript
var ok = scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
if (ok) console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
else console.warn('PR body update failed — summary comment still posted');
return !!ok;
```

### Thread 5 — `js/common/pullRequest.js` line 203

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION (repost, still valid): `pr.merged === true` is unreachable; ADO `completed` state not covered**

Carrying this over from the previous round — it was not addressed and remains accurate:

- `github_list_prs` (REST list) returns no `merged` field and only `state: 'open'` PRs are listed, so `if (pr.merged === true) return true;` never fires in production — the `ai_validating` label is the only live freeze signal. Harmless defensive code, but a one-line comment saying so would stop readers hunting for the populating call site.
- ADO closes work items/PRs as `completed`, which `state === 'closed' || state === 'merged'` does not match — if this predicate is ever fed ADO-shaped state, it won't freeze. Worth a comment or an explicit `'completed'` arm.

Non-blocking; the shipped behavior is correct for the GitHub path this guards.

## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

2. **Dead seam.** The rewrite being frozen lives in `updatePullRequestBody` behind `scm.updatePrBody` — but no SCM provider implements `updatePrBody` (checked `_createGithubProvider`, `_createGitLabProvider`, `_createAdoProvider` in `js/common/scm.js`; the string appears only in this consumer and in test mocks). In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

I also searched the rest of the tree: no JS code path edits an existing PR body (merge bot, smAgent, pushReworkChanges, developTicketAndCreatePR, postMobileTestAutomationResults all only *read* bodies or post comments). That means the `Closes #952` line landed on #956's body at the merge moment from outside the JS automation — most plausibly an agent session in the finalizing run editing the body via `gh` (the rework/dev legs have `bash` in `CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` and produce `outputs/pr_body.md`).

**Ask:** trace the actual write path for dev PRs and put the freeze there — e.g. a pre/post-JS guard that refuses `gh pr edit --body*` while `ai_validating` is on the PR, or a prompt-level rule in the rework/dev instructions. Alternatively, implement `updatePrBody` on the GitHub provider so the machine owns the body rewrite deterministically and this guard becomes live code. As shipped, the ticket AC ("the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms") is not demonstrably satisfied.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):

This PR ships 9 files under `.fah/memory/` (7 agent memory notes, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`) that have nothing to do with gh-960 — they are `fa` session memory records (dated 2026-10-03/04, topics: development-agent loop gotchas, CI secret-handling notes) captured by the WIP auto-save. `main` deliberately does not track `.fah/` (`.gitignore` line 36, reinforced by b8d09c4e "chore: ignore .fah/ session runtime artifacts"), and this PR itself deletes the sibling `.fah/bash_jobs/*` artifacts as noise.

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `updatePullRequestBody` reports success even when the PATCH fails**

Now that `scm.updatePrBody` is a live seam (gh-960 rework implemented `_githubUpdatePrBody`), it returns `null` when the `gh api` PATCH throws or yields no output — but this caller logs `✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result` and returns `true` regardless:

if (scm.updatePrBody) {
    scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
    console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
    return true;
}
```

Non-blocking (the return value isn't consumed and failures stay non-fatal by design), but a `null` result printing a green check is misleading in logs. Consider:

```javascript

if (ok) console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
else console.warn('PR body update failed — summary comment still posted');

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):

Carrying this over from the previous round — it was not addressed and remains accurate:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #983._

> ℹ️ **2 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 3 — `.fah/memory/.gitignore` line 1

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: session memory artifacts leaked into the PR — remove `.fah/memory/`**

This PR ships 9 files under `.fah/memory/` (7 agent memory notes, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`) that have nothing to do with gh-960 — they are `fa` session memory records (dated 2026-10-03/04, topics: development-agent loop gotchas, CI secret-handling notes) captured by the WIP auto-save. `main` deliberately does not track `.fah/` (`.gitignore` line 36, reinforced by b8d09c4e "chore: ignore .fah/ session runtime artifacts"), and this PR itself deletes the sibling `.fah/bash_jobs/*` artifacts as noise.

Beyond scope creep, these files will keep causing exactly the kind of merge friction this PR is already hitting (a live session mutates its memory/jobs state while another branch deletes it). Drop them from the PR (`git rm -r --cached .fah/memory` + commit; keep the working-tree copies locally).

Note: no literal secret is exposed in these notes (the PUSH_TOKEN mention describes interpolation, not a value), but session memory still does not belong in the shared repo tree.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/postTestReworkResults.js` line 279

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `updatePullRequestBody` reports success even when the PATCH fails**

Now that `scm.updatePrBody` is a live seam (gh-960 rework implemented `_githubUpdatePrBody`), it returns `null` when the `gh api` PATCH throws or yields no output — but this caller logs `✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result` and returns `true` regardless:

```javascript
if (scm.updatePrBody) {
    scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
    console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
    return true;
}
```

Non-blocking (the return value isn't consumed and failures stay non-fatal by design), but a `null` result printing a green check is misleading in logs. Consider:

```javascript
var ok = scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
if (ok) console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
else console.warn('PR body update failed — summary comment still posted');
return !!ok;
```

---

### Thread 5 — `js/common/pullRequest.js` line 203

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION (repost, still valid): `pr.merged === true` is unreachable; ADO `completed` state not covered**

Carrying this over from the previous round — it was not addressed and remains accurate:

- `github_list_prs` (REST list) returns no `merged` field and only `state: 'open'` PRs are listed, so `if (pr.merged === true) return true;` never fires in production — the `ai_validating` label is the only live freeze signal. Harmless defensive code, but a one-line comment saying so would stop readers hunting for the populating call site.
- ADO closes work items/PRs as `completed`, which `state === 'closed' || state === 'merged'` does not match — if this predicate is ever fed ADO-shaped state, it won't freeze. Worth a comment or an explicit `'completed'` arm.

Non-blocking; the shipped behavior is correct for the GitHub path this guards.

---


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 3 — `.fah/memory/.gitignore` line 1

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: session memory artifacts leaked into the PR — remove `.fah/memory/`**

This PR ships 9 files under `.fah/memory/` (7 agent memory notes, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`) that have nothing to do with gh-960 — they are `fa` session memory records (dated 2026-10-03/04, topics: development-agent loop gotchas, CI secret-handling notes) captured by the WIP auto-save. `main` deliberately does not track `.fah/` (`.gitignore` line 36, reinforced by b8d09c4e "chore: ignore .fah/ session runtime artifacts"), and this PR itself deletes the sibling `.fah/bash_jobs/*` artifacts as noise.

Beyond scope creep, these files will keep causing exactly the kind of merge friction this PR is already hitting (a live session mutates its memory/jobs state while another branch deletes it). Drop them from the PR (`git rm -r --cached .fah/memory` + commit; keep the working-tree copies locally).

Note: no literal secret is exposed in these notes (the PUSH_TOKEN mention describes interpolation, not a value), but session memory still does not belong in the shared repo tree.

### Thread 4 — `js/postTestReworkResults.js` line 279

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `updatePullRequestBody` reports success even when the PATCH fails**

Now that `scm.updatePrBody` is a live seam (gh-960 rework implemented `_githubUpdatePrBody`), it returns `null` when the `gh api` PATCH throws or yields no output — but this caller logs `✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result` and returns `true` regardless:

```javascript
if (scm.updatePrBody) {
    scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
    console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
    return true;
}
```

Non-blocking (the return value isn't consumed and failures stay non-fatal by design), but a `null` result printing a green check is misleading in logs. Consider:

```javascript
var ok = scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
if (ok) console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
else console.warn('PR body update failed — summary comment still posted');
return !!ok;
```

### Thread 5 — `js/common/pullRequest.js` line 203

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION (repost, still valid): `pr.merged === true` is unreachable; ADO `completed` state not covered**

Carrying this over from the previous round — it was not addressed and remains accurate:

- `github_list_prs` (REST list) returns no `merged` field and only `state: 'open'` PRs are listed, so `if (pr.merged === true) return true;` never fires in production — the `ai_validating` label is the only live freeze signal. Harmless defensive code, but a one-line comment saying so would stop readers hunting for the populating call site.
- ADO closes work items/PRs as `completed`, which `state === 'closed' || state === 'merged'` does not match — if this predicate is ever fed ADO-shaped state, it won't freeze. Worth a comment or an explicit `'completed'` arm.

Non-blocking; the shipped behavior is correct for the GitHub path this guards.

## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

I also searched the rest of the tree: no JS code path edits an existing PR body (merge bot, smAgent, pushReworkChanges, developTicketAndCreatePR, postMobileTestAutomationResults all only *read* bodies or post comments). That means the `Closes #952` line landed on #956's body at the merge moment from outside the JS automation — most plausibly an agent session in the finalizing run editing the body via `gh` (the rework/dev legs have `bash` in `CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` and produce `outputs/pr_body.md`).

**Ask:** trace the actual write path for dev PRs and put the freeze there — e.g. a pre/post-JS guard that refuses `gh pr edit --body*` while `ai_validating` is on the PR, or a prompt-level rule in the rework/dev instructions. Alternatively, implement `updatePrBody` on the GitHub provider so the machine owns the body rewrite deterministically and this guard becomes live code. As shipped, the ticket AC ("the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms") is not demonstrably satisfied.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 3 — `.fah/memory/.gitignore` line 1

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: session memory artifacts leaked into the PR — remove `.fah/memory/`**

This PR ships 9 files under `.fah/memory/` (7 agent memory notes, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`) that have nothing to do with gh-960 — they are `fa` session memory records (dated 2026-10-03/04, topics: development-agent loop gotchas, CI secret-handling notes) captured by the WIP auto-save. `main` deliberately does not track `.fah/` (`.gitignore` line 36, reinforced by b8d09c4e "chore: ignore .fah/ session runtime artifacts"), and this PR itself deletes the sibling `.fah/bash_jobs/*` artifacts as noise.

Beyond scope creep, these files will keep causing exactly the kind of merge friction this PR is already hitting (a live session mutates its memory/jobs state while another branch deletes it). Drop them from the PR (`git rm -r --cached .fah/memory` + commit; keep the working-tree copies locally).

Note: no literal secret is exposed in these notes (the PUSH_TOKEN mention describes interpolation, not a value), but session memory still does not belong in the shared repo tree.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/postTestReworkResults.js` line 279

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `updatePullRequestBody` reports success even when the PATCH fails**

Now that `scm.updatePrBody` is a live seam (gh-960 rework implemented `_githubUpdatePrBody`), it returns `null` when the `gh api` PATCH throws or yields no output — but this caller logs `✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result` and returns `true` regardless:

```javascript
if (scm.updatePrBody) {
    scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
    console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
    return true;
}
```

Non-blocking (the return value isn't consumed and failures stay non-fatal by design), but a `null` result printing a green check is misleading in logs. Consider:

```javascript
var ok = scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
if (ok) console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
else console.warn('PR body update failed — summary comment still posted');
return !!ok;
```

---

### Thread 5 — `js/common/pullRequest.js` line 203

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION (repost, still valid): `pr.merged === true` is unreachable; ADO `completed` state not covered**

Carrying this over from the previous round — it was not addressed and remains accurate:

- `github_list_prs` (REST list) returns no `merged` field and only `state: 'open'` PRs are listed, so `if (pr.merged === true) return true;` never fires in production — the `ai_validating` label is the only live freeze signal. Harmless defensive code, but a one-line comment saying so would stop readers hunting for the populating call site.
- ADO closes work items/PRs as `completed`, which `state === 'closed' || state === 'merged'` does not match — if this predicate is ever fed ADO-shaped state, it won't freeze. Worth a comment or an explicit `'completed'` arm.

Non-blocking; the shipped behavior is correct for the GitHub path this guards.

---


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

2. **Dead seam.** The rewrite being frozen lives in `updatePullRequestBody` behind `scm.updatePrBody` — but no SCM provider implements `updatePrBody` (checked `_createGithubProvider`, `_createGitLabProvider`, `_createAdoProvider` in `js/common/scm.js`; the string appears only in this consumer and in test mocks). In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 3 — `.fah/memory/.gitignore` line 1

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: session memory artifacts leaked into the PR — remove `.fah/memory/`**

This PR ships 9 files under `.fah/memory/` (7 agent memory notes, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`) that have nothing to do with gh-960 — they are `fa` session memory records (dated 2026-10-03/04, topics: development-agent loop gotchas, CI secret-handling notes) captured by the WIP auto-save. `main` deliberately does not track `.fah/` (`.gitignore` line 36, reinforced by b8d09c4e "chore: ignore .fah/ session runtime artifacts"), and this PR itself deletes the sibling `.fah/bash_jobs/*` artifacts as noise.

Beyond scope creep, these files will keep causing exactly the kind of merge friction this PR is already hitting (a live session mutates its memory/jobs state while another branch deletes it). Drop them from the PR (`git rm -r --cached .fah/memory` + commit; keep the working-tree copies locally).

Note: no literal secret is exposed in these notes (the PUSH_TOKEN mention describes interpolation, not a value), but session memory still does not belong in the shared repo tree.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/postTestReworkResults.js` line 279

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `updatePullRequestBody` reports success even when the PATCH fails**

Now that `scm.updatePrBody` is a live seam (gh-960 rework implemented `_githubUpdatePrBody`), it returns `null` when the `gh api` PATCH throws or yields no output — but this caller logs `✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result` and returns `true` regardless:

```javascript
if (scm.updatePrBody) {
    scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
    console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
    return true;
}
```

Non-blocking (the return value isn't consumed and failures stay non-fatal by design), but a `null` result printing a green check is misleading in logs. Consider:

```javascript
var ok = scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
if (ok) console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
else console.warn('PR body update failed — summary comment still posted');
return !!ok;
```

---

### Thread 5 — `js/common/pullRequest.js` line 203

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION (repost, still valid): `pr.merged === true` is unreachable; ADO `completed` state not covered**

Carrying this over from the previous round — it was not addressed and remains accurate:

- `github_list_prs` (REST list) returns no `merged` field and only `state: 'open'` PRs are listed, so `if (pr.merged === true) return true;` never fires in production — the `ai_validating` label is the only live freeze signal. Harmless defensive code, but a one-line comment saying so would stop readers hunting for the populating call site.
- ADO closes work items/PRs as `completed`, which `state === 'closed' || state === 'merged'` does not match — if this predicate is ever fed ADO-shaped state, it won't freeze. Worth a comment or an explicit `'completed'` arm.

Non-blocking; the shipped behavior is correct for the GitHub path this guards.

---


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

2. **Dead seam.** The rewrite being frozen lives in `updatePullRequestBody` behind `scm.updatePrBody` — but no SCM provider implements `updatePrBody` (checked `_createGithubProvider`, `_createGitLabProvider`, `_createAdoProvider` in `js/common/scm.js`; the string appears only in this consumer and in test mocks). In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

I also searched the rest of the tree: no JS code path edits an existing PR body (merge bot, smAgent, pushReworkChanges, developTicketAndCreatePR, postMobileTestAutomationResults all only *read* bodies or post comments). That means the `Closes #952` line landed on #956's body at the merge moment from outside the JS automation — most plausibly an agent session in the finalizing run editing the body via `gh` (the rework/dev legs have `bash` in `CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` and produce `outputs/pr_body.md`).

**Ask:** trace the actual write path for dev PRs and put the freeze there — e.g. a pre/post-JS guard that refuses `gh pr edit --body*` while `ai_validating` is on the PR, or a prompt-level rule in the rework/dev instructions. Alternatively, implement `updatePrBody` on the GitHub provider so the machine owns the body rewrite deterministically and this guard becomes live code. As shipped, the ticket AC ("the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms") is not demonstrably satisfied.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 3 — `.fah/memory/.gitignore` line 1

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: session memory artifacts leaked into the PR — remove `.fah/memory/`**

This PR ships 9 files under `.fah/memory/` (7 agent memory notes, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`) that have nothing to do with gh-960 — they are `fa` session memory records (dated 2026-10-03/04, topics: development-agent loop gotchas, CI secret-handling notes) captured by the WIP auto-save. `main` deliberately does not track `.fah/` (`.gitignore` line 36, reinforced by b8d09c4e "chore: ignore .fah/ session runtime artifacts"), and this PR itself deletes the sibling `.fah/bash_jobs/*` artifacts as noise.

Beyond scope creep, these files will keep causing exactly the kind of merge friction this PR is already hitting (a live session mutates its memory/jobs state while another branch deletes it). Drop them from the PR (`git rm -r --cached .fah/memory` + commit; keep the working-tree copies locally).

Note: no literal secret is exposed in these notes (the PUSH_TOKEN mention describes interpolation, not a value), but session memory still does not belong in the shared repo tree.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/postTestReworkResults.js` line 279

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `updatePullRequestBody` reports success even when the PATCH fails**

Now that `scm.updatePrBody` is a live seam (gh-960 rework implemented `_githubUpdatePrBody`), it returns `null` when the `gh api` PATCH throws or yields no output — but this caller logs `✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result` and returns `true` regardless:

```javascript
if (scm.updatePrBody) {
    scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
    console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
    return true;
}
```

Non-blocking (the return value isn't consumed and failures stay non-fatal by design), but a `null` result printing a green check is misleading in logs. Consider:

```javascript
var ok = scm.updatePrBody(prNumber, body);
if (ok) console.log('✅ Updated PR/MR body with latest test rework result');
else console.warn('PR body update failed — summary comment still posted');
return !!ok;
```

### Thread 5 — `js/common/pullRequest.js` line 203

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION (repost, still valid): `pr.merged === true` is unreachable; ADO `completed` state not covered**

Carrying this over from the previous round — it was not addressed and remains accurate:

- `github_list_prs` (REST list) returns no `merged` field and only `state: 'open'` PRs are listed, so `if (pr.merged === true) return true;` never fires in production — the `ai_validating` label is the only live freeze signal. Harmless defensive code, but a one-line comment saying so would stop readers hunting for the populating call site.
- ADO closes work items/PRs as `completed`, which `state === 'closed' || state === 'merged'` does not match — if this predicate is ever fed ADO-shaped state, it won't freeze. Worth a comment or an explicit `'completed'` arm.

Non-blocking; the shipped behavior is correct for the GitHub path this guards.

## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

2. **Dead seam.** The rewrite being frozen lives in `updatePullRequestBody` behind `scm.updatePrBody` — but no SCM provider implements `updatePrBody` (checked `_createGithubProvider`, `_createGitLabProvider`, `_createAdoProvider` in `js/common/scm.js`; the string appears only in this consumer and in test mocks). In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

I also searched the rest of the tree: no JS code path edits an existing PR body (merge bot, smAgent, pushReworkChanges, developTicketAndCreatePR, postMobileTestAutomationResults all only *read* bodies or post comments). That means the `Closes #952` line landed on #956's body at the merge moment from outside the JS automation — most plausibly an agent session in the finalizing run editing the body via `gh` (the rework/dev legs have `bash` in `CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` and produce `outputs/pr_body.md`).

**Ask:** trace the actual write path for dev PRs and put the freeze there — e.g. a pre/post-JS guard that refuses `gh pr edit --body*` while `ai_validating` is on the PR, or a prompt-level rule in the rework/dev instructions. Alternatively, implement `updatePrBody` on the GitHub provider so the machine owns the body rewrite deterministically and this guard becomes live code. As shipped, the ticket AC ("the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms") is not demonstrably satisfied.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.
